notes: Offshore structures are subject to marine biofouling, which increases the surface roughness and thus loads on the structures. This dataset provides high-resolution point clouds of cylinders overgrown by marine biofouling, enabling analysis through spatial statistics. The dataset contains point clouds of eleven stainless steel cylinders positioned in the Jade Bight and submerged for 28-29 months for biofouling to populate the surfaces. The cylinders were 65 cm long and varied in diameter (D = 27.3; 10.2 cm). The cylinders were positioned at two pontoons, A and B, approximately 1 and 2 km from the shoreline, respectively. Each pontoon was equipped with six cylinders. The cylinders were permanently submerged at least 1.0 m below the water surface. One cylinder got lost due to heavy corrosion. Point clouds were generated using close-range structure-from-motion (SfM) photogrammetry using hand-held cameras. Each point cloud was generated from 191 – 350 photographs with an overlap of >90%. L and I-shaped reference bars were placed around each sample to aid 3D reconstruction. Image processing and 3D model reconstruction were performed using Agishoft Metashape Professional (v2.0.1). The point clouds consist of 2435216 – 3771036 and 4502453 – 5599009 points for the cylinders with diameters of 10.2 and 27.3 cm, respectively.
